patient_summary:
Hello there! I'll explain what's happening and what you need to do next in simple terms.

You had a surgery to remove your tonsils and adenoids. Your doctor did this to help with your sore throat and to fix some problems with your nose.

Here's what you need to do:

1. Take Lortab (a pain medicine) as directed. Follow the instructions on the bottle.
2. Take amoxicillin (another medicine) as directed. Follow the instructions on the bottle.
3. Use Ponaris nose drops as directed. Follow the instructions on the bottle.

These medicines will help with any pain and to keep your throat and nose from getting infected.

If you have any of these symptoms, call your doctor right away:
- If you have a fever
- If you have a lot of pain
- If you have trouble breathing
- If you have bleeding from your nose
- If you have a lot of drainage from your nose

Remember, it's important to follow your doctor's instructions and to call if you have any questions or if you're not feeling well. Your doctor and nurses are here to help you.
caregiver_checklist: Give the patient Lortab as prescribed.
Give the patient amoxicillin as prescribed.
Check the patient’s temperature, pulse, and respiration every hour for the first 6 hours.
Watch for signs of infection such as fever, redness, or increased pain.
Call if the patient has a fever over 100.4°F (38°C).
Schedule a follow-up appointment in 3-4 weeks.
Check for any bleeding or drainage from the nose.
Watch for signs of nasal congestion or discharge.
Call if the patient has persistent nasal congestion or discharge.
Schedule a follow-up appointment in 3-4 weeks.
Check for any signs of infection such as fever, redness, or increased pain.
Call if the patient has persistent signs of infection.
child_explanation: You had a little operation today, sweetie. The doctors took out your swollen tonsils and adenoids. They also cleaned your nose a bit. You'll be okay, and the grown-ups are taking really good care of you. You'll get some medicine to help you feel better. The doctors will check on you tomorrow and in a few weeks. You're doing great, you're strong!
source_text: PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSES,1.  Recurrent tonsillitis.,2.  Deeply cryptic hypertrophic tonsils with numerous tonsillolith.,3.  Residual adenoid hypertrophy and recurrent epistaxis.,POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSES,1.  Recurrent tonsillitis.,2.  Deeply cryptic hypertrophic tonsils with numerous tonsillolith.,3.  Residual adenoid hypertrophy and recurrent epistaxis.,FINAL DIAGNOSES,1.  Recurrent tonsillitis.,2.  Deeply cryptic hypertrophic tonsils with numerous tonsillolith.,3.  Residual adenoid hypertrophy and recurrent epistaxis.,OPERATION PERFORMED,1.  Tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy.,2.  Left superficial nasal cauterization.,DESCRIPTION OF OPERATION:,  The patient was brought to the operating room.  Endotracheal intubation carried out by Dr. X. The McIvor mouth gag was inserted and gently suspended.  Afrin was instilled in both sides of the nose and allowed to take effect for a period of time.  The hypertrophic tonsils were then removed by the suction and snare.  Deeply cryptic changes as expected were evident.  Bleeding was minimal and controlled with packing followed by electrocautery followed by extensive additional irrigation.  An inspection of the nasopharynx confirmed that the adenoids were in fact hypertrophic rubbery cryptic and obstructive.  They were shaved back, flushed with prevertebral fascia with curette.  Hemostasis established with packing followed by electrocautery.  In light of his history of recurring nosebleeds, both sides of the nose were carefully inspected.  A nasal endoscope was used to identify the plexus of bleeding, which was predominantly on the left mid portion of the septum that was controlled with broad superficial cauterization using a suction cautery device.  The bleeding was admittedly a bit of a annoyance.  An additional control was established by infiltrating slowly with a 1% Xylocaine with epinephrine around the perimeter of the bleeding site and then cauterizing the bleeding site itself.  No additional bleeding was then evident.  The oropharynx was reinspected, clots removed, the patient was extubated, taken to the recovery room in stable condition.  Discharge will be anticipated later in the day on Lortab plus amoxicillin plus Ponaris nose drops.  Office recheck anticipated if stable and doing well in three to four weeks.
